newsitem.title: CHINA: China brewery eyes domestic convertible bond issue.
newsitem.headline: China brewery eyes domestic convertible bond issue.

text.p: China's Guangzhou Zhujiang Brewery Group Co aims to issue convertible bonds worth 360 million yuan pending regulatory approval, a company official said on Friday.
The bonds will be convertible into stock, pushing Zhujiang Brewery to eventually list on one of China's two stock markets in Shenzhen and Shanghai, she said.

The brewery is waiting for the green light from the China Securities Regulatory Commission, China's top securities authority, to go ahead with the offer, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter the China Securities Bulletin.
China in April announced a four billion yuan quota for convertible bonds, which would be used by some of the country's top 500 state-run but non-listed enterprises.
Beijing has said the size of each convertible bond offer must be a minimum of 100 million yuan and the bonds must have a term of no less than three years and no more than five years.
Zhujiang Brewery, based in Guangzhou, capital of southern Guangdong province, aims to use the proceeds to boost brewing capacity and buy other domestic breweries, the official said.
Zhujiang plans to push its annual beer production capacity to 1.4 million tonnes by the year 2000 from the present 350,000 tonnes, she said.
She declined to give further details on the bond issue.
Zhujiang has forecast net profits of more than 70 million yuan for 1997 against 68 million yuan in 1996, she said.
Zhujiang expected to sell 350,000 tonnes of beer this year, up from 258,000 in 1996, the official said.
